title: Why Can't You Lick Your ELBOW? 💪
description:
Can you lick your elbow? Go on, try it (gently). Almost nobody can, and it's not because your tongue is too short. Your upper arm is one stiff bone, pinned at your shoulder, so your elbow can only swing round your shoulder in a circle, like a compass. And your mouth sits INSIDE that circle: the elbow can go round it, or past it, but never quite in. The rare few who can usually have a long tongue, short upper arms (or very bendy shoulders).
Could you reach it? Yes or no?

Numbers: an adult's shoulder-to-elbow length is about 33 to 37 cm, while the mouth is only about 25 to 30 cm from the shoulder joint (a rough estimate from average body measurements), and the tongue sticks out only a few centimetres past the lips.

Bonus: the pointy bit you were aiming for isn't even your upper arm. It's the top of your forearm bone, the ulna (the olecranon).
